title: Accelerating Dynamic Network Embedding with Billions of Parameter Updates to Milliseconds

problem.claim: Dynamic graphs are challenging for network embedding methods to accommodate in practice.

gap.claim: Existing node-by-node embedding modifications face a tradeoff between efficient calculation and accuracy.

contributions.claim: A dynamic network embedding paradigm updates the embedding-space axes through rotation and scaling instead of node-by-node updates.

The Dynamic Adjacency Matrix Factorization algorithm performs dynamic network embedding by rotating and scaling the coordinate system, with no more node-embedding changes than the number of edge modifications.
A dynamic Personalized PageRank procedure enhances the obtained node embeddings and captures higher-order neighbor information dynamically.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the dynamic network embedding paradigm based on rotating and scaling embedding-space axes as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on node classification, link prediction, and graph reconstruction across different-sized dynamic graphs suggest that DAMF advances dynamic network embedding.
On billion-edge graphs, DAMF updates billion-level parameters in less than 10 milliseconds.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dynamic graphs create practical challenges for network embedding.
Node-by-node embedding modifications struggle to balance computational efficiency and accuracy.
The proposed paradigm rotates and scales embedding-space axes rather than updating nodes individually.
DAMF implements this approach, and dynamic Personalized PageRank adds higher-order neighbor information.
The authors report gains across several graph tasks and sub-10-millisecond updates for billion-edge graphs.

source_observation.claim: The method changes the embedding-space coordinate system instead of modifying node embeddings one by one.

interpretation.claim: When representation dimension is much smaller than graph size, global low-dimensional transformations may reduce update costs.

application.claim: For dynamic graph systems, consider coordinate-system transformations when per-node updates are too costly.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when the transformation preserves accuracy or fails under particular graph dynamics.

unknowns: Exact datasets, baselines, metrics, and comparative results are not specified.
The hardware and update workload underlying the reported less-than-10-millisecond result are not specified.
The abstract does not provide theoretical guarantees or reproducibility details.
